extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of Euclid's Elements; learners of classical Euclidean geometry (Book VI)
extracted.subtask_description: Excerpts of Euclid Book VI: propositions and problems about figures 'given in species', ratios between sides/figures, and constructions to find or compare magnitudes and ratios among triangles, parallelograms, and other rectilineal figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XLIX — Triangle given in species when one angle and combined ratio of two sides to third is given
rubrics_metrics.description: If a triangle has one angle given, and if the sides about another angle, both together, have a given ratio to the third side; the triangle is given in species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof/construction: bisect the specified angle, reduce the given combined ratio to a ratio of segments on the base (using prior propositions), determine one of the sub-triangles given in species, recover the full angle by doubling the bisected angle, and construct the triangle. The text includes a worked procedure (take EFG as given angle, use prop. 44 to find EFL, make LEM equal to FEL, locate intersection of produced lines) showing how to construct such a triangle and why the ratio condition holds.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. L — Line from vertex in given angle has given ratio to base
rubrics_metrics.description: If from the vertex of a triangle given in species, a straight line be drawn to the base in a given angle; it shall have a given ratio to the base.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the triangle is given in species the constituent angles are known, so the subtriangle formed by the drawn line is given in species and its side ratios to the base are therefore given. The proof reduces the ratio AD:BC to known ratios AD:AB and AB:BC.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. LI — Rectilineal figures given in species divide into triangles given in species
rubrics_metrics.description: Rectilineal figures given in species, are divided into triangles which are given in species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction/proof: join nonadjacent vertices to partition the polygon into triangles. Since the figure is given in species, relevant angles and ratios are given, so each triangle formed (e.g., BAE, BED, BDC) is shown to be given in species by referenced data and prior propositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. LII — Two triangles given in species on same base have given ratio
rubrics_metrics.description: If two triangles given in species be described upon the same straight line; they shall have a given ratio to one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: construct equiangular triangles on an arbitrary reference line matching corresponding angles to reduce the ratio of triangles to the ratio of certain constructed straight segments. The text includes a problem: taking FG as reference, build triangles equiangular to the given ones and find ratio LF:FK which equals triangle ABC:ABD.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. LIII — Two rectilineal figures given in species on same base have given ratio
rubrics_metrics.description: If two rectilineal figures given in species be described upon the same straight line; they shall have a given ratio to one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses division into triangles (join diagonals), find ratios of component triangles by previous data, then compose ratios by addition/composition to obtain ratio of whole rectilineal figures. A constructive problem shows how to build a reference straight line with segments in the same composed ratios leading to HM:MO representing the requested ratio.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. LIV — Similar figures on proportional lines have given ratio
rubrics_metrics.description: If two straight lines have a given ratio to one another; the similar rectilineal figures described upon them, similarly, shall have a given ratio to one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take a third proportional to the given lines to reduce the figure-ratio to a ratio of straight lines, then use similarity: as AB:CD :: CD:G, hence figure E:figure F is given. Problem: construct auxiliary segments H,K,L to realize the same ratio and show E:F = H:L.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. LV — Figures given in species on lines with given ratio have given ratio
rubrics_metrics.description: If two straight lines have a given ratio to one another; the rectilineal figures given in species described upon them, shall have to one another a given ratio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct on one line a figure similar and similarly placed to the figure on the other line; use that figures given in species on the same line have given ratio (prop. 53) and that similar figures on proportionals have given ratio (prop. 54) to deduce the desired ratio. Problem: use a reference line H and find K,L so H:L equals E:F.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. LVI — Figure given in species on given straight line is given in magnitude
rubrics_metrics.description: If a rectilineal figure given in species be described upon a straight line given in magnitude; the figure is given in magnitude.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct a square on the given straight line (square is given in species and magnitude). Since the figure and square are on the same given line, their ratio is given; combined with the known magnitude of the square, deduce magnitude of the figure. Problem: replicate line GH = AB and transfer ratios to obtain parallelogram equal to given figure.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. LVII (labelled LVH) — Given ratios of one pair of homologous sides determine the rest
rubrics_metrics.description: If two rectilineal figures are given in species, and if a side of one of them has a given ratio to a side of the other; the ratios of the remaining sides to the remaining sides shall be given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using known ratios within each given figure (sides of each have given ratios) and the given cross-ratio AB:DE, deduce BC:EF etc by composition and chain of proportionalities. A constructive method uses an arbitrary reference line and stages of proportional construction to find the required ratios explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. LVIII — Homologous sides of similar figures inherit given ratio
rubrics_metrics.description: If two similar rectilineal figures have a given ratio to one another, their homologous sides have also a given ratio to one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let G be third proportional to homologous sides CD,EF; since figure A:B is given, deduce CD:G and hence CD:EF given. Construction: take an arbitrary H, apply ratio H:K equal to A:B and find mean proportional to get the side-ratio H:L equal to CD:EF.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. LIX — Sides of figures given in species with given figure-ratio have given side-ratios
rubrics_metrics.description: If two rectilineal figures given in species have a given ratio to one another, their sides shall likewise have given ratios to one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If figures are similar use previous proposition. If not similar, construct on a side of one a figure similar to the other so that chosen sides are homologous; since both figures are given in species their ratio is given, and the similarity yields the side ratio. Constructively, choose reference H, make ratios H:K and K:L, find mean proportional M and get side ratio H:M representing CD:EF.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. LX — Sides of figure given in species and magnitude are given in magnitude
rubrics_metrics.description: If a rectilineal figure be given in species and magnitude, the sides of it shall be given in magnitude.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place a figure similar to the given one upon a given straight line BC; that constructed figure is given in species on a given line so is given in magnitude; homology yields the magnitude of the corresponding side EF and similarly for all sides. Problem: describe figure similar to D and equal to H by constructing appropriate parallelograms and mean proportionals (refs to earlier propositions).

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. LXI — Parallelogram given in magnitude with one side and one angle given: other side given
rubrics_metrics.description: If a parallelogram given in magnitude has one of its sides and one of its angles given in magnitude, the other side also is given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct a parallelogram equal to the given one on a given straight line EF with the given angle, then use reciprocal proportionality of sides about equal angles to deduce the unknown side AC from AB:EF :: EG:AC. The construction yields AC as a given magnitude.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. LXII — Rectangle contained by sides about a given angle has a given ratio to parallelogram
rubrics_metrics.description: If a parallelogram has a given angle, the rectangle contained by the sides about that angle has a given ratio to the parallelogram.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drop a perpendicular from a vertex to form triangle(s) so that the ratio BA:AE is given; then as BA:AE so is rectangle AB·BC to AE·BC (i.e., rectangle to parallelogram) giving the required ratio. Corollary: triangle-based rectangle also has a given ratio to the triangle when angle is given, with method of constructing FGK and relating GF:FK to the rectangle:triangle ratio.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. LXIII — For equiangular parallelograms, sides and parallelogram ratios relate reciprocally
rubrics_metrics.description: If two parallelograms be equiangular, as a side of the first to a side of the second, so is the other side of the second to the straight line to which the other side of the first has the same ratio which the first parallelogram has to the second (and conversely).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce and construct parallelogram BGHC to achieve reciprocal proportionality, show BH equals DF, and deduce AB:BG :: AC:DF. Use this to translate a parallelogram ratio to a side ratio and vice versa. The proposition also gives how knowledge of one ratio yields the other.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. LXIV — Parallelograms with unequal but given angles: given parallelogram ratio gives side ratio
rubrics_metrics.description: If two parallelograms have unequal but given angles, and if as a side of the first to a side of the second, so the other side of the second be made to a certain straight line; if the ratio of the first parallelogram to the second be given, the ratio of the other side of the first to that straight line shall be given (and conversely).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct at B an angle equal to the given angle of the second parallelogram, complete parallelogram KBCL, and use equalities/equiangularity and prior data to deduce KB:M ratios and hence AB:M. The corollary extends to triangles with equal or unequal but given angles.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. LXV — Eqiangular parallelograms: given parallelogram ratio plus one side ratio gives the other side ratio
rubrics_metrics.description: If two equiangular parallelograms have a given ratio to one another, and if one side has to one side a given ratio; the other side shall also have to the other side a given ratio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given AB:EF and parallelogram AB:CD known, construct supporting line EG to which AB corresponds; infer AE:CF by composing proportionalities: as EB:FD :: FC:EG and AE:EG given, deduce AE:CF. A constructive method using reference segments H,K,L is provided to compute AE:CF.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. LXVI — Parallelograms with unequal but given angles and a given parallelogram ratio: knowing one side ratio gives the other side ratio
rubrics_metrics.description: If two parallelograms have unequal, but given angles, and a given ratio to one another; if one side has to one side a given ratio, the other side has also a given ratio to the other side.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At B construct angle equal to the given angle and parallelogram KBLC; use that triangle ABK is given in species to know AB:BK, combine with known ratios of parallelograms and sides (BL:EG etc.) to deduce AB:EF. A constructive method with reference line MN and segments MO:OP demonstrates finding the desired ratio.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. LXVII — Eqiangular parallelograms: given ratios of sides imply given parallelogram ratio
rubrics_metrics.description: If the sides of two equiangular parallelograms have given ratios to one another; the parallelograms shall have a given ratio to one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take an arbitrary K and set K:L equal to AB:EF and L:K equal to BC:FG to obtain M; since parallelogram ratio equals straight-line ratio, K:M corresponds to parallelogram AC:EG. Use composition to conclude the parallelogram ratio is given. The proposition provides a constructive scheme using chosen reference segments to compute the parallelogram ratio from side ratios.
